architecture_layer: Frontend Responsive Shell — off-canvas mobile navigation, icon-only desktop collapse, and mobile-first view layout

chain.reason: the cumulative change is 720 authored lines against a 400-line hard limit, and it mixes two independent invariants with different rollback boundaries
chain.recommendation: land as two commits, newest last
chain.unit_1: responsive shell: off-canvas navigation below md, mobile-first grids, word breaking, table min-widths, document viewport contract
chain.unit_2: icon-only collapsible sidebar on desktop, with persisted preference
chain.caveat: frontend/components/Sidebar.tsx contains hunks from both units, so splitting it needs a manual hunk split rather than a path split
chain.commits_made: none — the maintainer has not asked for a commit

causal_invariants.statement: On a viewport narrower than 768px the operator can reach every navigation destination and no view forces horizontal scrolling, because the sidebar is off-canvas below md and no fixed-width chrome or unbreakable content exceeds the viewport.
On a viewport of 768px or wider the operator can reclaim the full content width by collapsing the sidebar to icons, and the choice survives a reload.

issue_pr.issue: none — no issue tracker entry exists for this work
issue_pr.pr: none — not opened; no commit requested by the maintainer

operator_flows.flow: Open the platform on a phone and reach a view from the navigation
operator_flows.expectation: sidebar starts off-canvas, aria-expanded=false on the toggle; activating it reveals the navigation
operator_flows.negative_control: navigation and main content both stay in the DOM; collapsing never unmounts a destination

operator_flows.flow: Pick a destination on a phone and read the resulting view
operator_flows.expectation: navigation collapses, aria-expanded=false, onNavigate fired exactly once
operator_flows.negative_control: scrim tap and Escape also collapse it

operator_flows.flow: Read a long GCS path in the training log or the ingestion target preview
operator_flows.entry: TrainingView ODD console, IngestionView upload dropzone
operator_flows.expectation: unbreakable paths wrap instead of forcing horizontal scroll inside a vertical scroller
operator_flows.negative_control: the console keeps its own vertical scrolling; wrapping adds no second scrollbar

operator_flows.flow: Focus a form control on iOS Safari
operator_flows.entry: tap a select or input below the md breakpoint
operator_flows.expectation: the viewport does not zoom in on focus and stay zoomed
operator_flows.negative_control: at 768px and above the 16px floor does not apply, so desktop density is unchanged

operator_flows.flow: Reclaim content width on a desktop window
operator_flows.entry: activate the panel control in the sidebar header
operator_flows.expectation: the panel narrows to icons only and reports aria-expanded=false; a second activation restores the labels
operator_flows.negative_control: every destination keeps its accessible name while collapsed, so a screen reader can still identify each icon

operator_flows.flow: Return to the platform after collapsing the panel
operator_flows.negative_control: an expanded preference is remembered as expanded; the off-canvas drawer state is unaffected by the collapse preference

journey_runtime_evidence.note: No gentle-ai-bench journey applies: this work adds no CLI or lifecycle flow. The drawer and collapse states are observable through the ARIA contract, so they are covered by real rendering tests rather than style assertions. Visual verification at 375px and at a collapsed desktop width was NOT performed — no browser automation is available here — so breakpoint appearance is reasoned from the emitted CSS, not observed.

seams_under_test.seam: app/layout.tsx module exports (metadata, viewport, RootLayout) — the contract App Router consumes to emit <head>

AppShell component — the operator-visible navigation contract expressed as ARIA: the mobile toggle aria-expanded and aria-controls, the collapse control aria-expanded, and the notification that navigation happened
seams_under_test.note: The seam is the ARIA state, not a CSS class, so the tests survive a restyle. Deliberately no test asserts a Tailwind class name anywhere.

seams_under_test.seam: Sidebar destinations — every destination must stay nameable by assistive technology in both the expanded and the icon-only state, and the panel control must report the current state
seams_under_test.note: This seam exists because collapsing to icons is the change most likely to silently destroy an accessible name: the visible label is hidden, and only the icon would remain.

tests.red_evidence: AppShell drawer: suite failed to resolve the module. Layout: 4 of 6 failed reading 'width'/'initialScale'/'viewportFit'/'themeColor' of undefined. Collapse: all 15 Sidebar/AppShell collapse tests failed because no collapse control existed. Preference: 'remembers a panel the operator had already collapsed' failed until the preference store existed.
harness_defects_found_and_fixed: window.matchMedia is undefined under this jsdom, which proved the shell capability guard is load-bearing rather than decorative
a media-query notification inside a test needs act() or the assertion runs before React flushes
the persisted collapse preference leaked across tests, so the AppShell suite now clears localStorage in beforeEach
the feedback counter arrives through a promise, so the assertion must use findByText rather than getByText
tests.product_defect_caught_by_a_test: The first collapse implementation read localStorage and called setState inside an effect, which introduced a new react-hooks/set-state-in-effect error. It was replaced with useSyncExternalStore over localStorage rather than suppressed, which also removed a ref-based write guard and added cross-tab synchronization through the storage event.
tests.not_tested_and_why: No test asserts a Tailwind class name. Verifying a className tests implementation, not behavior. Instead every class authored here was verified to be emitted in the built CSS, which catches typos and dead utilities without coupling tests to styling. Note that grepping the built CSS requires the escaped class form and fixed-string matching, or valid utilities appear to be missing.

phase_0_gitignore_invariant.defect: root .gitignore rule 'lib/' (unanchored) excluded frontend/lib/ at any depth, leaving the API clients and schemas untracked
phase_0_gitignore_invariant.resolved_by: the RF_06 task, merged as commit 0bda3bb
phase_0_gitignore_invariant.verified: git check-ignore -v frontend/lib/api.ts exits 1; git ls-files frontend/lib returns all 7 files
phase_0_gitignore_invariant.residual_risk: the unanchored 'lib/' rule still matches any future directory named lib at any depth; the negation only rescues frontend/lib exactly

odd_observability_features.navigation_state_contract: aria-expanded on the mobile toggle and on the panel control are the single source of truth for reachability, asserted at the component seam
odd_observability_features.preference_persistence: localStorage key fama:sidebar-collapsed, read through useSyncExternalStore so a second browser tab follows the change via the storage event
odd_observability_features.resilience_observability: the shell degrades to a usable layout where window.matchMedia is unavailable, and to an expanded panel where localStorage throws
odd_observability_features.note: The TrainingView banners, connection state machine and exponential backoff were left untouched.

unresolved_authority_decisions: No visual verification was performed at 375px or at a collapsed desktop width; no browser automation is available. A maintainer should eyeball both states on a real device before shipping.

The 16px mobile form-control floor in globals.css is a global change that inflates every control below 768px. It is the correct fix for the iOS focus zoom, but it shifts layout in tight rows and needs a device check.
Sidebar.tsx mixes hunks from both chain units, so the split needs a manual hunk split.
IngestionView still uses animate-in and zoom-in-95, confirmed dead in the built CSS because tailwindcss-animate is not installed. Pre-existing, untouched.

PredictionView and IngestionView dropzones advertise drag and drop but have no onDragOver or onDrop handler, only onClick, so drag and drop cannot work on touch devices. Pre-existing and out of scope.

The 9 pre-existing react-hooks/set-state-in-effect errors (DashboardView 133/144, IngestionView 238, PredictionView 196/227/440/531) were deliberately left alone; they are state-shape problems, not layout problems, and deserve their own work unit.

rollback.unit_1: git checkout -- frontend/app frontend/components/views && restore Sidebar.tsx and page.tsx to pre-chain state
rollback.unit_2: the collapse is a single self-contained slice: revert Sidebar.tsx icon-only rendering, the two collapse fields in AppShell, the two new props wired in page.tsx, and localStorage key fama:sidebar-collapsed is then unused
